topic: Broker Office Management, Branch Offices & Recordkeeping
question: May a Pennsylvania broker open a branch office without first obtaining a separate license for that location?
choice_a: No -- a branch office license must be obtained from the Commission before opening
choice_b: Yes, as long as the main office is properly licensed
choice_c: Yes, but only for offices located within the same county
choice_d: No branch office license exists in Pennsylvania; only the broker's individual license matters
explanation: 49 Pa. Code Section 35.243(a) states that a broker or cemetery broker may not open a branch office in Pennsylvania without first obtaining a branch office license for that location from the Commission, submitted with the fee prescribed in Section 35.203.
source_note: 49 Pa. Code Section 35.243(a) (confirmed verbatim via pacodeandbulletin.gov)

topic: Broker Office Management, Branch Offices & Recordkeeping
question: Under what name is a Pennsylvania branch office license issued?
choice_a: Any trade name the branch manager chooses, independent of the main office
choice_b: The same name under which the broker is licensed to conduct business at the main office
choice_c: The name of the associate broker assigned to run that location
choice_d: A name that must differ from the main office to avoid confusion
explanation: 49 Pa. Code Section 35.243(b) requires the branch office license to be issued in the name under which the broker or cemetery broker is licensed to conduct business at the main office -- branch offices cannot operate under a separate, unapproved trade name.

topic: Broker Office Management, Branch Offices & Recordkeeping
question: What happens to a Pennsylvania branch office license if the broker's main license is suspended or revoked?
choice_a: The branch office may continue operating under the supervising associate broker
choice_b: The branch office has 90 days to find a new broker of record before termination
choice_c: The branch office license terminates automatically
choice_d: Nothing changes -- branch and main licenses are entirely independent
explanation: 49 Pa. Code Section 35.243(c) provides that a branch office license terminates automatically with the suspension, revocation, or discontinuance, for whatever reason, of the license of the broker to whom the branch office license was issued.

topic: Broker Office Management, Branch Offices & Recordkeeping
question: Who must be present to supervise and direct the main or branch office of a Pennsylvania broker?
choice_a: Any licensed salesperson designated in writing by the firm
choice_b: A property manager, whether licensed or not
choice_c: No supervisory license is required at the branch level, only at the main office
choice_d: A broker or associate broker holding a standard or reciprocal license
explanation: 49 Pa. Code Section 35.244(a) requires the main or branch office of a broker to be under the direction and supervision of a broker or associate broker holding either a standard or reciprocal license -- an unlicensed manager cannot fill this role.

topic: Broker Office Management, Branch Offices & Recordkeeping
question: Under 49 Pa. Code Section 35.244(d), in what manner is a branch office prohibited from operating?
choice_a: In a manner that permits, or is intended to permit, an employee to carry on the business of the office for the employee's sole benefit
choice_b: In a manner that allows evening or weekend hours
choice_c: In a manner that permits remote work by licensed salespersons
choice_d: In a manner that allows co-branding with an affiliated mortgage company
explanation: 49 Pa. Code Section 35.244(d) specifically prohibits operating a branch office in a way that permits, or is intended to permit, an employee to carry on the office's business solely for that employee's own personal benefit rather than under genuine broker supervision.

topic: Broker Office Management, Branch Offices & Recordkeeping
question: What are Pennsylvania's physical requirements for a broker's main office under 49 Pa. Code Section 35.242?
choice_a: It must occupy a minimum of 500 square feet of dedicated commercial space
choice_b: It must be devoted to the transaction of real estate business, arranged to permit business to be conducted in privacy, and (if in a residence) have separate entrance access
choice_c: It must be located within the same municipality as the broker's residence
choice_d: It must be open to walk-in clients a minimum of 40 hours per week
explanation: Section 35.242 requires the office to be devoted to real estate business and arranged for private client conversations; if the office is located in a residence, it must have a separate entrance, and the business name must be prominently and permanently displayed outside.
source_note: 49 Pa. Code Section 35.242 (confirmed via pacodeandbulletin.gov summary of office requirements)

topic: Broker Office Management, Branch Offices & Recordkeeping
question: For how long must a Pennsylvania broker generally retain records pertaining to a real estate transaction?
explanation: 49 Pa. Code Section 35.286(a) requires a broker or cemetery broker to retain transaction records for at least 3 years following consummation, consistent with RELRA Section 604(6), which lists failing to preserve 3 years of records as a disciplinary violation.
source_note: 49 Pa. Code Section 35.286(a); 63 P.S. Section 455.604(6) (both confirmed)

topic: Broker Office Management, Branch Offices & Recordkeeping
question: Which category of consumer-notice acknowledgment is subject to a SHORTER retention period (6 months) rather than the general 3-year rule under 49 Pa. Code Section 35.286?
choice_d: The acknowledgment portion of certain consumer disclosure notices when there is no resulting real estate transaction
explanation: Section 35.286(a)(1)-(4) carves out certain consumer-notice acknowledgments -- such as the disclosure summary acknowledgment when no transaction resulted, time-share disclosure acknowledgments, lease disclosure acknowledgments, and subagent/transaction-licensee disclosure statements -- for a shorter 6-month retention period rather than the general 3-year rule.

topic: Broker Office Management, Branch Offices & Recordkeeping
question: Who is responsible for producing a broker's records for examination when the Commission conducts an office inspection?
choice_a: The broker (or, for an entity, the corporation/partnership/association whose records they are)
choice_b: Only the individual salesperson involved in the specific transaction under review
choice_d: No one -- Commission inspectors may not compel record production without a subpoena
explanation: 49 Pa. Code Section 35.286(b) places the duty to produce records for Commission examination -- whether upon written request or during an office inspection under Section 35.246 -- on the broker or cemetery broker, and separately on the entity itself if a corporation, partnership, or association holds the license.

topic: Broker Office Management, Branch Offices & Recordkeeping
question: May a licensed salesperson independently negotiate or execute a lease on behalf of a lessor while assisting a broker with property management?
choice_a: Yes, provided the salesperson has at least 1 year of experience
choice_b: No -- the salesperson's property management work must be supervised and controlled by the employing broker, and the salesperson may not independently negotiate or execute the lease
choice_c: Yes, without restriction, once the salesperson is affiliated with any broker
choice_d: Only associate brokers, never salespersons, may perform property management tasks at all
explanation: 49 Pa. Code Section 35.287 permits a salesperson to assist in property management only if the work is supervised and controlled by the employing broker, and expressly bars the salesperson from independently negotiating lease terms or executing a lease on the lessor's behalf.

topic: Broker Office Management, Branch Offices & Recordkeeping
question: What must a Pennsylvania broker do before a proposed trade or business name may be used for the brokerage?
choice_a: Simply begin using the name and update the Commission only if a complaint is later filed
choice_b: Register the name only with the IRS, with no state-level approval needed
choice_c: Obtain approval through the license/branch application process with the Commission before using the name
choice_d: Nothing -- Pennsylvania places no restrictions on brokerage trade names
explanation: Because a branch or main office license is issued in the name under which the broker is authorized to do business (49 Pa. Code Section 35.243(b)), any proposed business or trade name must be reflected in and approved through the Commission's licensing/application process rather than adopted unilaterally.
source_note: 49 Pa. Code Section 35.243(b) (confirmed); general Commission licensing-application practice

topic: Broker Office Management, Branch Offices & Recordkeeping
question: May a rental listing referral agent supervise more than one office in Pennsylvania?
choice_b: Yes, with no limit, as long as each office has a sign-in log
choice_c: Yes, but only if each office is within the same ZIP code
choice_d: No -- a rental listing referral agent may not supervise more than one office
explanation: 49 Pa. Code Section 35.244(e) requires a rental listing referral agent office to be under the direction of a rental listing referral agent holding a standard or reciprocal license, and expressly caps that agent's supervisory role at one office.

topic: Broker Office Management, Branch Offices & Recordkeeping
question: An associate broker, salesperson, or other individual licensee must practice in affiliation with what, under 49 Pa. Code Section 35.244(c)?
choice_a: A broker holding a reciprocal or standard license issued by the Commission
choice_b: Any real estate trade association of the licensee's choosing
choice_c: A title insurance company approved by the Commission
choice_d: No affiliation requirement exists once a license is issued
explanation: Section 35.244(c) requires an associate broker, salesperson, cemetery salesperson, campground membership salesperson, or time-share salesperson to practice in affiliation with a broker holding either a reciprocal or standard Commission-issued license -- reinforcing that non-broker licensees cannot operate independently.

topic: Broker Office Management, Branch Offices & Recordkeeping
question: Which of the following is a broker of record's core statutory responsibility when the license is held by a corporation, partnership, or association?
choice_a: Serving strictly as a rainmaker who is not personally accountable for salesperson conduct
choice_b: Being the individual broker who independently satisfies the qualification and application requirements and who is responsible for the entity's real estate transactions
choice_c: Holding the license temporarily until any associate broker is ready to take over
choice_d: Being exempt from the broker's education and experience requirements because the entity itself is licensed
explanation: RELRA Section 513 requires that, when a corporation, partnership, or association applies for a broker's license, the individual designated as broker of record must independently meet Sections 511 and 512's qualification and application requirements, and 49 Pa. Code Section 35.201 defines that individual as responsible for the entity's real estate transactions.
source_note: 63 P.S. Section 455.513; 49 Pa. Code Section 35.201 (both confirmed)

topic: Broker Office Management, Branch Offices & Recordkeeping
question: Which RELRA disciplinary provision specifically targets a broker's failure to exercise adequate supervision over the office's licensed salespersons or associate brokers?
explanation: RELRA Section 604(16) makes it grounds for discipline when, 'in the case of a broker licensee, failing to exercise adequate supervision over the activities of his licensed salespersons or associate brokers within the scope of this act' -- directly linking office management failures to license suspension, revocation, or fines.
source_note: 63 P.S. Section 455.604(16) (confirmed verbatim via legis.state.pa.us RELRA full text)

topic: Broker Office Management, Branch Offices & Recordkeeping
question: Does Pennsylvania require a broker to physically display real estate licenses in the office?
choice_a: No -- Pennsylvania abolished license-display requirements in 1990
choice_b: Only digital display on a website satisfies the requirement
choice_c: Only the broker of record's license, not salespersons' licenses, must be displayed
choice_d: Yes -- 49 Pa. Code Subchapter C addresses the display of licenses in the office as part of its office-requirement provisions
explanation: 49 Pa. Code Section 35.245 ('Display of licenses in office'), part of Subchapter C's office-requirement provisions alongside general office requirements, branch licensure, supervision, and office inspection, requires licenses to be displayed at the office where the licensee practices.
source_note: 49 Pa. Code Section 35.245 (confirmed to exist via the Chapter 35 subchapter C table of contents on pacodeandbulletin.gov; title and placement confirmed, full subsection text not independently pulled in this pass)

topic: Broker Office Management, Branch Offices & Recordkeeping
question: If a Pennsylvania sole-proprietor broker becomes seriously ill or injured, what regulatory mechanism exists to keep the brokerage functioning?
choice_a: 49 Pa. Code Section 35.254 provides for substitution of the broker or broker of record due to illness or injury
choice_b: The brokerage must immediately cease all operations until the broker recovers
choice_c: Any salesperson in the office may automatically assume the broker's authority with no Commission involvement
choice_d: The Commission automatically revokes the license after 30 days of the broker's incapacity
explanation: 49 Pa. Code Section 35.254 ('Substitution of broker or broker of record due to illness or injury'), found within Subchapter C's 'Status of Licensure' provisions, addresses exactly this contingency, alongside related provisions for a deceased sole-proprietor broker's business (Section 35.252) and broker-of-record replacement due to death (Section 35.253).
source_note: 49 Pa. Code Chapter 35, Subchapter C table of contents, Section 35.254 (confirmed to exist and its title via pacodeandbulletin.gov; full subsection text not independently pulled in this pass)
